question: In standard IVF (without ICSI), fertilisation is achieved by injecting a single spermatozoon directly into the oocyte cytoplasm under a microscope.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Standard IVF places a prepared sperm suspension around the oocyte and allows fertilisation to occur naturally. Direct injection of a single sperm into the oocyte cytoplasm is the technique used in ICSI, which is specifically indicated for severe male factor infertility.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. In standard IVF, retrieved oocytes are inseminated by placing approximately 50,000–100,000 prepared sperm around each oocyte; fertilisation is left to occur naturally. It is ICSI (intracytoplasmic sperm injection) that involves direct injection of a single sperm into the oocyte.
